extracted.intended_audience: photojournalists, photographers, videographers and professionals interested in submitting work to or attending the Visa pour l'Image festival
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and criteria related to awards, grants, exhibitions, content classification, and submission/opportunity information for the Visa pour l'Image international photojournalism festival.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canon Female Photojournalist Grant (eligibility & purpose)
rubrics_metrics.description: For the 26th consecutive year, Canon is awarding the Canon Female Photojournalist Grant to a female photographer in recognition of her contribution to photojournalism. The grant is worth 8,000 euros, provided by Canon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility implied: female photographers; purpose is recognition of contribution to photojournalism; financial award amount (8,000€) and deadline are relevant (page shows '9 days until closing'). No further selection criteria given on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canon Video Grant - Short Film Documentary (eligibility & support)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Canon Short Video Documentary Grant is designed to support a videographer and/or photographer by awarding a grant of 8,000 euros, funded by Canon, as well as the loan of a video kit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target applicants: videographers and/or photographers working on short film documentaries; support includes monetary award (8,000€) and loaned equipment (video kit). Deadline timing is shown on the page ('17 days until the deadline'). No detailed judging criteria published here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visa d’or franceinfo Award for the Best Digital News Story (format & evaluative focus)
rubrics_metrics.description: Virtual reality, interactivity, video, and social media posts… In the face of a constant flow of information, the franceinfo Digital Information Gold Award recognizes a project, piece of content, or creative work that offers a fresh perspective on the news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepts digital formats (VR, interactivity, video, social media). Core evaluative criterion stated: the work must offer a 'fresh perspective on the news.' Deadline indicator present ('31 days until the deadline').

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibition thematic categories (classification/selection areas)
rubrics_metrics.description: The festival organizes exhibitions around themes listed/used as filters: conflicts, environment, social issues, tech, culture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exhibitions are categorized by theme for selection/display and for visitors filtering; these themes reflect topical areas the festival highlights when curating work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content suitability labeling for exhibitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Content is labeled for audience suitability with categories shown on the page: 'Not suitable for a young audience' and 'Suitable for all ages'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a content-rating/filtering criterion for exhibitions (the page shows counts: Not suitable for a young audience (4), Suitable for all ages (9)). Curators and submitters should expect age-appropriateness to be considered and displayed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show your work — submission & professional-development opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Would you like to show your reportage or simply get advice on your work? Whether you're a young or experienced photojournalist, Visa pour l'Image is a unique opportunity to meet international photo editors and professionals from the world of the press and photojournalism. Options listed: Submit a project, Portfolios, Meetings, Workshops.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied criteria/guidance: both emerging and experienced practitioners are welcome; submissions and portfolio reviews are opportunities to obtain editorial feedback and exposure. The page lists types of engagement (project submission, portfolio meetings, workshops) but does not give technical submission rules here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalistic quality standards emphasized in editorial
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial by Jean-François Leroy argues that journalism and professional photographers supply the reliable, up-to-date, verified data necessary for truth — and that media which adhere to standards and rules produce 'real photos' and valuable reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly values: reliability, up-to-date information, verification, adherence to professional standards and rules, legitimacy and influence. These are presented as core qualities that distinguish trustworthy journalism/photojournalism from manipulated or fake content — implied selection/curation criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional reputation and editorial distribution as a quality signal
rubrics_metrics.description: The editorial highlights the success and digital offerings of major outlets (The New York Times, Le Monde, the Financial Times) and suggests their influence and legitimacy act as bulwarks against misinformation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied evaluative dimension: provenance and publication venue (established media organizations) contribute to perceived credibility and may factor into how work is valued or promoted by the festival or its discourse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadlines / timeliness for calls for entries
rubrics_metrics.description: The page displays time-until-deadline indicators for calls (e.g., '9 days until closing', '17 days until the deadline', '31 days until the deadline').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeliness is a practical requirement for submission eligibility. Applicants must meet posted deadlines; the festival signals urgency on call pages. No further procedural deadlines/details are provided on this page.
